title: Parts of the pistol
subtitle: The semi-automatic pistol: main parts and what they do

lines: In this episode, we learn the main parts of the semi-automatic pistol, and what each one does.
To properly understand how a handgun works, you must first be familiar with its parts and their functions.

scenes.heading: What you must be able to do
bullets: Label the diagram of a pistol or a revolver
lines: By the end of this module, you must be able to label the diagram of either a semi-automatic pistol or a revolver.
You must also be able to explain four terms, starting with the frame.
Then the barrel.
Then the slide, or on a revolver, the cylinder.
And finally, the action.

scenes.definition: The body of the firearm to which all the other parts are attached.
lines: The frame is the body of the firearm to which all the other parts are attached.
The book compares it to the chassis of a motor vehicle.

lines.text: On our pistol, this is the frame.
All the other parts are attached to it.
And this is the barrel.
The barrel is a metal tube down which the bullet will travel.

scenes.definition: Spiraling lands and grooves inside the barrel that cause the bullet to spin.
lines: Inside the barrel there are spiraling lands and grooves, known as rifling.
The rifling causes the bullet to spin.
This spinning stabilises the bullet in flight.

lines.text: Now the slide.
The slide usually works on a blowback principle.
It relies on the pressure created by the cartridge firing sequence.
This pressure, after pushing the bullet forward, will push the slide to the rear.
During the slide's rearward movement, it will eject the fired case and cock the hammer.
On its forward movement, the slide will pick up a new cartridge from the magazine and push it into the chamber.
The action refers to the moving parts of the firearm.
For example, the trigger.
The hammer.
And the slide.
Page twenty four labels the parts of the semi-automatic pistol.
The muzzle and the front sight.
The slide, the slide lock, and the rear sight.
The hammer and the safety catch.
The frame, the trigger guard and the trigger.
Then the grip, and the magazine release.
The photo of the pistol taken apart also labels the barrel and the chamber.
And the magazine.

scenes.heading: The book's labelled pistol
scenes.caption: Parts of the semi-automatic pistol, p. 24
lines: Here is the book's photo, with fourteen labels.
Two of these parts aren't on our drawing.
The hammer spur, on the hammer.
And the tang.
Learn all fourteen names.
The formative exam asks you to label the diagram of either a semi-automatic pistol or a revolver, for fourteen marks.

scenes.heading: A disassembled semi-automatic pistol
scenes.caption: A disassembled semi-automatic pistol, p. 24
lines: This photo shows the pistol taken apart.
At the top is the slide, with the rear sight and the front sight.
Below it, the barrel, with the chamber at one end and the muzzle at the other.
Then the recoil guide and spring.
The frame, with the slide lock shown on its own.
On the frame, the hammer spur, hammer, tang, trigger, trigger guard, grip and magazine release are labelled again.
And the magazine, and the magazine well.

scenes.heading: Glock semi-automatic pistol
scenes.caption: Glock semi-automatic pistol, p. 25
lines: Page twenty five shows a Glock semi-automatic pistol, with its magazine out.
Most of its labels you already know.
One is new: the trigger safety, on the trigger.

scenes.source: Handgun manual, p. 23; formative exam, p. 75
scenes.question: What is the frame?
options: The metal tube the bullet travels down
The body to which all other parts are attached
The moving parts of the firearm
lines: The exam asks you to explain the frame.
Which of these is the frame?
reveal: The frame is the body of the firearm to which all the other parts are attached.

scenes.source: Handgun manual, p. 23; formative exam, p. 75
scenes.question: What does the action refer to?
options: The moving parts of the firearm
lines: The exam also asks about the action.
What does the action refer to?
reveal: The action refers to the moving parts of the firearm, for example the trigger, the hammer and the slide.

points: Frame: the body all parts attach to
lines: The frame is the body, and all the other parts are attached to it.
The barrel's rifling makes the bullet spin, which stabilises it in flight.
The slide is pushed to the rear, ejecting the fired case and cocking the hammer, and on its way forward it pushes a new cartridge into the chamber.
The action is the moving parts: trigger, hammer and slide.
And learn the labels on page twenty four.
